title: Condorium
tagline: A committee of LLM agents that judges ideas in two rounds and is built, in code, not to flatter you.
problem: A single LLM asked to judge an idea tends to agree with the person asking, drifts with the tone of the pitch and averages away the real objections. That makes LLM feedback on ideas cheap but hard to trust.
approach: A LangGraph pipeline runs seven role agents in a blind first round, then a deliberation round where each sees every other opinion and must justify any revision. Guardrails are code, not prompts: the most enthusiastic score is capped at the others' median + 3, citations must come from papers retrieved during the run, and the synthesis reports disagreements instead of an average. Runs are checkpointed in SQLite and resumable.

limits: The anti-leak cleaner is lexical: a paraphrased victory clue survives (kept as a strict xfail test).
Benchmark pairs are synthetic and few: 3 pairs over 1 seed(s) completed (NIM free-tier rate limits, budget < 2,000 calls); a one-pair difference is within noise.
With this model the debate fired on every idea; the gap >= 3 trigger may be too loose.
The demo GIF is a replay of a recorded run, not a live computation.
One open model (via NIM) was measured; other providers are untested here.
